blocks.text: Re: Trademark Clearance for Jackson Inc
Dear Ms. Hunter:

This letter sets out the terms on which our firm will act for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} in clearing the trademarks it proposes to adopt, and it becomes our agreement once you countersign it and return a copy to me. I have written the terms out at some length and in plain words, because a clearance engagement runs more smoothly when both sides have read the same description of the work before it starts, and because the value of a clearance search lies as much in the limits we draw around it as in the searching itself. Please read what follows against your own understanding of what you have asked us to do, and telephone me before you sign if any part of it does not match what you expect of us.
The Work We Will Do

The engagement is a trademark clearance directed at the marks that Jackson Inc has identified to us for use with its goods and services, and its purpose is to assess the risk that adopting and using each proposed mark would conflict with rights already held by others. We will search the federal register, the records of the state registries, and the common-law sources available to us for marks that are the same as or confusingly similar to each candidate, read what those searches return against the goods and services you intend to offer, and give you our assessment of the risk each candidate carries together with the options that assessment leaves open to you. Where a conflict is close enough that reasonable people could weigh it differently, we will say so plainly rather than resolve the question more firmly than the record will bear.

It is worth stating with equal care what this engagement is not. Our clearance is an assessment of the marks and classes you identify and the records our searches reach as of the date we report, and it is neither a guarantee that no conflicting right exists beyond what those searches surface, nor an opinion on the validity of any registration we happen to find, nor a filed application, unless we later agree in writing to take that further step. If you add candidate marks, widen the goods and services, or ask us to extend the search beyond the United States, we will scope and price that additional work before we begin it, so that nothing is added to this engagement without your agreement to it.
Conflicts of Interest

Before opening this matter we ran our conflicts check, and it turned up nothing that prevents us from acting for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} on this clearance. If a conflict later comes to light, we will tell you at once and will not carry the matter forward until we have addressed it with you, because clearing that question at the outset costs far less than untangling it in the middle of the work.
Who Will Do the Work

Ashley Williams, a patent agent in our prosecution group, will run the searches and build the analysis that supports our assessment, and she will be your team's day-to-day contact on the substance of the work. Kelly Snyder, an associate in the same group, will maintain the search record, keep the matter anchored to our docket, and prepare the written clearance report that carries our conclusions to you. Anything that turns on a judgment about the risk a given conflict presents is reviewed by me before it reaches you, so that the assessment you rely on carries the firm's name and not one person's alone, and the people whose names are on the work are the people who have done it.
Fee and Start Date

Our fee to {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} for the clearance described above is {{fact:f:E-2024-001.fee}}, fixed for that scope rather than billed against hourly time, so that you can put a candidate mark to us without watching a clock. We will begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2024-001.start}}, and we plan on roughly four months from that date to the written clearance report, though we will tell you early if the work turns out to need more time or less. If you ask us to widen the scope, we will quote the addition in writing and will not start it until you have agreed the price.
Invoicing and Payment

We will bill the fixed fee in installments as the work proceeds, and each invoice is due within thirty days of its date. Out-of-pocket costs, chiefly the fees charged by the search services we use, are billed at cost and itemized on the invoice, and we do not mark them up. If an invoice goes unpaid past its due date, we may suspend work on the matter after written notice to you, because a clearance left half-finished serves no one, and we would rather pause it cleanly than carry it on unpaid.
Term and Termination

The engagement runs from the start date set out above until we deliver the written clearance report, unless either of us ends it sooner. Either party may end it on written notice, for any reason or none. If you end it, you owe the fee for the work performed to that date, prorated against the fixed fee, together with any costs we have incurred, and we will hand over the search record and our work in whatever state it has then reached.
Confidentiality

We will treat the marks you are weighing, the goods and services behind them, and the fact and terms of this engagement as confidential, and we will use what you tell us only to perform the work you have retained us for. A clearance touches brand decisions you have not yet made public, and we will handle it with that in mind. Our analysis and the correspondence around it are intended to be protected by the attorney-client privilege, and we ask that you keep them within the group at {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} that needs them, since a privileged assessment shared too widely can lose the protection that lets us write to you candidly.
Limitation of Liability

We will perform this engagement with the care and skill our profession expects, and our assessment will reflect our best professional judgment on the records before us. We cannot warrant a particular outcome, because a clearance turns on the rights of others and on how a court or the trademark office might one day weigh them, and those are matters no counsel controls. Our total liability arising out of this engagement, on any theory, is limited to the fee you actually pay us for it, except where the law does not permit that limit, and neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss, including lost profits.
Governing Law

This letter is the entire agreement between us on this engagement and supersedes anything discussed or drafted before it, and it may be changed only in a writing that we both sign. It is governed by the law of the state in which our firm keeps its principal office, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules, and any dispute we cannot settle between ourselves will be heard by the courts sitting in that state, whose jurisdiction we each accept.

If these terms match your understanding, please sign and date the enclosed copy of this letter and return it to me, and we will open the matter and begin on the date set out above. If you would rather talk any part of it through first, tell me and I will make the time this week.
Very truly yours,

To: Kelly Snyder, Matthew Parrish
From: Ashley Williams
Re: Kickoff -- Trademark Clearance for Jackson Inc

Our job on this one is narrow, and I want us to hold it that way. Jackson Inc has given us a set of proposed marks to clear before it commits to any of them, and the {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2024-001.start}}. We owe the client a clean search of each candidate and a written assessment of the risk it carries, and nothing that reads as a conclusion on that risk goes out without counsel's review.

We are at the very front of the work, so this memo sets the scope and the order of the searches, not any findings. There are no results yet, and there should not be. Read it as the plan of record for the matter, and tell me now if any of it does not fit how you expected the clearance to run.
How the work breaks down, in the order I expect us to run it

items: Fix the scope. I will pin down each candidate mark and the exact goods and services Jackson Inc means to use it on, from what Cynthia Hunter and her team send over. A mark cleared against the wrong class is not cleared at all, so this comes first and I will not rush it.

Knockout searches. I will run a first-pass search of each candidate against the federal register, to drop any that collide head-on before we spend the full search on it. This is a filter, not an opinion, and it stays that way in the file.

Full clearance search. For the marks that survive the knockout, I will search the federal register, the state registries, and the common-law sources, and pull every mark that reads as the same or confusingly similar. Matthew Parrish will take the state and common-law searches so we cover more ground in parallel rather than one source after another.

Record and report. Kelly Snyder keeps the search record current and anchored to the docket as we go, and she will build the written clearance report from it. The risk assessment in that report is reviewed by counsel before it reaches the client, not sent straight from the search results.

blocks.text: One rule while the matter is open. Anything that goes to Jackson Inc that touches a conclusion on risk goes through counsel first. We are agents on this clearance, and the view on whether a mark is safe to adopt is the firm's to give and to stand behind, so we hand it up rather than offer it ourselves. Routine questions about scope and materials I will take with Cynthia Hunter directly, and I will copy the two of you so the thread stays in one place.

Getting started this week: I will send Cynthia Hunter the short list of what we need to fix the scope, and Kelly Snyder will open the matter on the docket and stand up the search file. Matthew Parrish, start reading into the goods-and-services classes for the candidates so we are ready to search the moment the scope is set.
The first thing that has to happen is the scope. Nothing downstream is worth starting until each candidate mark and its classes are fixed in writing, so that is where our time goes now.
Good morning Cynthia,

I am opening this thread so that our updates on the trademark clearance stay in one place as the work moves. Where we stand: the scope is set, and I have the knockout searches underway against the federal register for each of the candidate marks Jackson Inc gave us. Keeping the status on this thread will keep it from scattering across separate notes.

For the file, I have Cynthia Hunter down as our single point of contact for the {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} clearance, so questions and approvals route to one place on your side. Kelly Snyder is keeping the search record current and anchored to our docket as the results come in.

One thing would help before we move to the full search. Please confirm the order in which you would like the candidates cleared, so that we spend the deep search on the marks that matter most to you first. None of this is a conclusion yet; the view on whether a given mark is safe to adopt comes in the written report, after counsel has reviewed it. A short reply is enough, or send me a couple of times for a call and I will set one up.
Regards
Cynthia,

Thank you for the quick turn on the class list. Ashley Williams has the knockout searches running against the federal register now, and I have opened the matter on our docket so that every search and date for the {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} clearance sits in one file. The docket also carries a check date for each search, so none of them can quietly drift.

One item is still open on our side. Two of the candidates you sent read close to marks already on the register, and we want to search those under their full goods-and-services descriptions before we say anything about them. That is search work, not a conclusion; the risk view on any candidate comes in the written report, after counsel has reviewed it.

Nothing is needed from you today. Our contact record shows Cynthia Hunter as the approver for the Jackson Inc clearance, so the next thing we bring you will be the knockout result, not another question. You should have that summary from Ashley Williams by the end of the week.
Best
Good morning Cynthia,

Good progress to report. The knockout searches are done, and most of the candidates came through the first pass clean. Two dropped out against marks already registered for close goods, which is exactly what the knockout stage is for, and we are moving the survivors into the full clearance search now.

Kelly Snyder has the search record current, so every candidate, class, and hit for the {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} clearance is captured in one place as we go. On the survivors, we are searching the federal register, the state registries, and the common-law sources together rather than one after another, so that we do not lose time.

One thing from you would help. For the two candidates that dropped, tell us whether Jackson Inc wants a substitute mark added to the search, so that we can fold it in now rather than open a second pass later. Our contact record shows Cynthia Hunter's approval of the search order, and we are following it. None of this is a conclusion yet; the view on whether each surviving mark is safe to adopt comes in the written report, after counsel has reviewed it.
Regards
Cynthia,

Confirmed, and thank you. The substitute mark is in, and Ashley Williams has added it to the full clearance search with the surviving candidates, so it clears on the same pass rather than a later one.

Timing on our side is unchanged. The full search for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} runs over the coming weeks, and the written clearance report follows once the searches are complete and counsel has reviewed the risk on each mark. The report will set out, for each surviving candidate, the conflicts the searches turned up and our read of the risk, with the options each one leaves open. I will flag anything that needs a decision from you as it comes up, and not before.
For the record, our file shows Cynthia Hunter as the approver for the Jackson Inc clearance, so we will bring the report to you when it is ready. Nothing is needed from you now.
Best
